resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (Certificate of Change in Ownership / Change in Occupancy), Borough Code Chapter 112
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Magnolia Construction Office (building inspector or housing inspector)
requirements: Home must meet the property maintenance standards the Borough adopted (BOCA National Property Maintenance Code, 1993) and all Borough ordinances
Hard-wired, interconnected smoke detectors with battery backup on or near the ceiling of each level
Battery smoke detectors in each bedroom or sleeping area
Smoke detectors must be certified by the fire official or other authorized person before the certificate is issued
Any repairs needed for the certificate are the current owner's responsibility, even if the problem was caused by a previous owner

Under Ordinance 12-2026 (adopted Sept 2, 2026) the owner stays responsible until the certificate is issued, no matter what the sale contract, settlement or escrow agreement says; each day of violation after notice is a separate offense

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Certificate of Continued Occupancy Application (linked from the Borough's "Certificate of Change in Occupancy" page, with an inspection checklist) and turn it in to the Construction Office, 438 W. Evesham Ave, Magnolia, with the $75.00 fee. An inspector will contact you to schedule. The owner or the owner's agent must apply.

resale_co.notes: Settled in round 3. The Borough code on Municode (Chapter 112, Certificates of Occupancy) requires a certificate before occupancy after a change of ownership, issued by the building or housing inspector, and Code 15.112-11 sets the fee for "Change of property ownership" of residential R1 to R4 and RS properties at $75.00. The Borough's own page (Internet Archive copy of Jan 11, 2026; live magnolia-nj.org is behind a Cloudflare check that was not bypassed) says the inspection is required whenever a home is sold and the form goes to the Construction Office with the $75.00 fee. The page moved from /certificate-change-ownership to /certificate-change-occupancy. Code 15.112-11 C: if violations are still not fixed after the first inspection and one reinspection, or the applicant misses the reinspection, the inspector may charge a reinspection fee equal to a new application. The Code also lists $150.00 for a "Certificate of continued occupancy, UCC permits may be required" and $50.00 per extension of a temporary CO; the $75.00 change-of-ownership fee is the one the Borough page quotes for home sales. Failure to comply: fine up to $500.00 per day (15.112-12). The application itself is an Adobe cloud link and the checklist file was not archived, so neither was read. Phone is the Borough Hall / Construction Office number listed in the DCA fire directory.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety is Magnolia's Uniform Fire Code enforcing agency ('S' = State in the July 2026 LEA Registry; Fire Official Louis Kilmer, NJ Div Fire Safety). However, on the DCA 'State Enforced Towns' list (revised 7/17/2026), Magnolia is listed WITHOUT the 'SC' (Smoke Certs) mark, while nearby Stratford and Woodlynne have it. The DCA fire directory lists the smoke detector compliance contact for Magnolia as the Magnolia Borough Construction Office, 438 West Evesham Ave, (856) 783-1520. So the smoke/CO/extinguisher certificate appears to be issued locally by the Borough, not by DCA. Fees and the application form could not be read because the Borough website is behind a Cloudflare check. A search summary of the Borough code (ecode360, not verified word for word) described a certificate of smoke detector compliance from the Borough fire official before occupancy, with fees based on time remaining before the change of occupant. Round 3: the Borough Code on Municode still contains Chapter 142 Article II (Ord. 2018-05), which made the Regional Fire Prevention Alliance (then based in Magnolia) the local enforcing agency and lists smoke/CO certificate fees of $56.00 (14 or more business days before settlement), $64.00 (8 to 13 days), $96.00 (4 to 7 days) and $161.00 (3 days or less), one reinspection included, certificate valid 90 days. That arrangement no longer matches the July 2026 DCA registry (Magnolia = State; the Alliance is now run by Barrington and does not list Magnolia), so these amounts are not recorded as current fees. Code 15.112-2 also says the Borough CO is issued only after the fire official (or other authorized person) certifies the smoke detectors, so the smoke check may be part of the $75.00 Borough inspection; confirm with the Construction Office.
